records.title: MobileBERT: a Compact Task-Agnostic BERT for Resource-Limited Devices
records.reason: MobileBERT is a directly relevant model-compression and inference-acceleration contribution for pretrained language models on mobile hardware, with measured Pixel 4 latency and size/speed gains. The full text identifies the model as bidirectional BERT used as a task encoder for fine-tuned NLP tasks, rather than an autoregressive generative LLM or its serving stack. It therefore sits at the boundary of the stated LLM inference scope and is retained as borderline.
records.body_check: Primary arXiv HTML full text reviewed: architecture and method (sections 2–3: deep/thin bottleneck BERT, inverted-bottleneck teacher, layer-wise knowledge transfer, and operational changes replacing LayerNorm/GELU), evaluation (section 4: GLUE and SQuAD quality, TensorFlow Lite on 4-thread Pixel 4 at sequence length 128; 25.3M parameters, 4.3x smaller and 5.5x faster than BERT_BASE; 8-bit quantization; latency ablations), and conclusion. The paper's evaluations are encoder/task metrics and fixed-input mobile latency, not autoregressive generation or LLM serving throughput. The conclusion reports the compact BERT result; no dedicated limitations section is present. Thus it demonstrates language-model compression/inference efficiency, but not specifically generative-LLM inference.

records.title: The Penn Treebank: Annotating Predicate Argument Structure
records.reason: The primary ACL proceedings record and paper abstract describe a syntactic/predicate-argument annotation scheme for the Penn Treebank corpus, including coindexed null elements and semantic-role tags to support parsing evaluation and training. This is a corpus and annotation contribution, not an LLM inference/serving system or an inference-time compression/efficiency technique. Abstract-level exclusion is sufficient for this clear scope mismatch.
records.body_check: The official ACL Anthology record (H94-1020) and primary PDF abstract were checked. They identify the paper as an annotation scheme and implementation for predicate-argument structure in the Penn Treebank; the described uses are parser comparison/training and linguistic analysis. This does not describe model inference, serving, or efficiency. Abstract/metadata evidence is sufficient for this clear exclusion; full text was not reviewed.

records.title: Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability
records.reason: The primary abstract studies grokking in small transformers trained on modular-addition tasks, reverse-engineers their Fourier-based algorithm, and defines measures of training progress through memorization, circuit formation, and cleanup. This is mechanistic interpretability and training-dynamics research, not an LLM inference/serving system or an inference-time compression/efficiency technique. Abstract-level exclusion is sufficient for this clear scope mismatch.
records.body_check: The primary arXiv record and abstract were checked. They explicitly limit the case study to small transformers trained on modular addition and examine learned mechanisms, weights/activations, Fourier-space ablations, and phases of training. No inference or serving optimization is claimed, so the paper is clearly outside scope and full text was not reviewed.
